summary: Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, University College London (~1841–1842), Charing Cross Hospital, and Imperial College School of Medicine (~1842–1845). He held a post at Imperial College London (~1854–1885).

Specializing in Sinology and Buddhist studies, Thomas James Mazanec studied at Calvin University, earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed his PhD at Princeton University under doctoral supervisors Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

Thomas Jülch specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, the University of Hull (MA), Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich (PhD), later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).
Thomas Kintaert works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Vienna, attested in 2009 and serving as a lecturer attested for 2022–2026.
Working in Indology and linguistics, Thomas M. Hunter served as a Dean at the University of Virginia and held a post at the University of British Columbia (attested 2011).

Thomas Nathan Patton specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

Working in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies, Thomas Oberlies studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held posts at Zurich (1990), Tübingen (attested 1988), Freiburg (attested 2001), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, Thomas R. Trautmann studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the University of Michigan, including as co-director attested in 1980 and attested in 1991.
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy (~1782–1784), Jesus College, Cambridge (1784), and the University of Cambridge (~1784–1788).

Thomas Roebuck worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at the Royal High School, he served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George (1811) and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1811–1819).
Thomas Watters specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Queen's University Belfast (1857–1861) and also studied at Queen's University of Ireland.
Thomas Zehnder works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich, studying under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang specialized in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Nanking under John Dewey and at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at National Central University (1925–1948) and National Taiwan University (~1948–1973).

Thubten Chodron works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan, and Dorje Pamo under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, and founded Sravasti Abbey (2003), where she serves as abbess.

Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as Professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1992) and as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.
Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under the 13th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche. His students included the 14th Dalai Lama, Thubten Jigme Norbu, Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa, and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Thubten Samphel worked in Tibetology, studying at St. Stephen's College (~1974–1977), the University of Delhi (~1974–1978), and Columbia University (~1981–1982). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thubten Yeshe worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and Geshe Rabten. He founded Kopan Monastery, Tushita Meditation Centre, and FPMT, and taught at the University of California, Santa Cruz (1977–1978).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Thubten Yeshe, Geshe Rabten, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He co-founded Kopan Monastery and FPMT, becoming its spiritual director in 1984, and founded Maitripa College.

Thupten Jinpa works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned a Geshe Lharam at Ganden Shartse and a B.A. at Cambridge, held posts at Cambridge and Stanford, and founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics.
